source_name: Singapore Statutes Online: Internal Security (Prohibition of Publications) (Consolidation) Order (Cap 143, s20; O 1; G.N. S 413/1950; 1990 RevEd)
locator: Citation/Prohibited publications (cl.2), extension note, Legislative History
decision_actor: Order originally G.N. S 413/1950 (Internal Security legislation, Singapore); extended to Singapore by L.N. 231 of 16.9.1963; 1990 Revised Edition operative 25 Mar 1992
measure: Printing, publication, sale, issue, circulation or possession of publications in the Schedule prohibited. The Schedule text is NOT shown on SSO web page; so title membership could not be verified from the primary source.
year_found: 1950 (original consolidation order); 1963 = only the date the ISA/order was extended to Singapore; 1992 = RevEd operative; NO title-level ban year found
status_now: Unclear. Internal Security order still shows as 'current' on SSO (16 Nov 2026). The 2015 de-gazetting concerned a DIFFERENT instrument (see correction). Wikipedia says 'banned under' the order but gives no lift; our 'lifted 2015' is unsupported for these titles.
correction: (a) The order: Internal Security (Prohibition of Publications) (Consolidation) Order, made as G.N. S 413/1950, under s.20 ISA, extended to Singapore 16 Sep 1963 (L.N. 231/1963), 1990 RevEd operative 25 Mar 1992. 1963 is NOT a ban date for any title. (b) Wikipedia's Singapore table cites only this SSO page for all 27 rows, a table shared 'banned under the order' with no years; the SSO page I could open does not show the Schedule, so title membership is unverified (Wikipedia likely drew on the Schedule PDF; not confirmed). (c) 2015 unban: MDA/MCI de-gazetted 240 publications effective 25 Nov 2015 (Undesirable Publications (Prohibition) Order 2015, S 721, made 20 Nov 2015, revoking the Undesirable Publications (Prohibition) (Consolidation) Order O 1 and GN 405 of 4 Feb 1994); 17 remained prohibited. That is the UNDESIRABLE PUBLICATIONS ACT 1967 regime, not the Internal Security order. News/IMDA coverage names anti-colonial, communist and adult titles (Dravida Nadu 1949, World Student News 1957, The Long March 1959, Fanny Hill 1966) but none of our Marxist titles are named in any source I could open. (d) No title-level date can be sourced.
suggested_note: Wikipedia's list of books banned by governments records this title as prohibited under Singapore's Internal Security (Prohibition of Publications) (Consolidation) Order (G.N. S 413/1950, extended to Singapore 1963); the Schedule date and any lifting could not be verified.
recommendation: year: CLEAR to null (1963 is the extension date of the instrument, not a ban decision). Remove 'lifted 2015' / status historical unless verified; set status unknown or 'reported', confidence reported. Note wording as in suggested_note. Do not cite the 2015 unban for these rows. If wanting certainty: obtain the Schedule via SSO PDF (print 'Print - PDF' of the 1990 RevEd) or ask AGC.
uncertainty: High. Could not retrieve the Schedule; individual title IDs were not matched by me (no id-to-title map available); verdict applies to the group. Straits Times article blocked.

correction: Start year is 1966 per Global Voices and a blog repost of the Straits Times piece, not 1948. End 2015 is right (240 de-gazetted, effective 25 Nov 2015). Legal regime: Undesirable Publications Act, not the Internal Security order.
suggested_note: Fanny Hill was on Singapore's list of prohibited publications from 1966 until the Media Development Authority de-gazetted it, with 239 other titles, on 25 November 2015.
uncertainty: Medium: 1966 comes from secondary reports (Global Voices, Straits Times via blog); I could not open the Straits Times or gazette.
